selector.champion: Primary invasive lobular breast carcinoma in heterotopic cutaneous breast tissue
selector.rationale: The presence of GATA3-positive and estrogen receptor–positive apocrine glands in close association to diffuse tumor cell infiltration, along with the histopathological features of dermal tumor infiltrating the subcutaneous fat without epidermal involvement and tumor cells lined up in an 'Indian file pattern', supports the diagnosis of primary invasive lobular breast carcinoma in heterotopic cutaneous breast tissue.

rejected.label: Hidradenocarcinoma
rejected.why: Lack of specific hidradenocarcinoma markers and presence of GATA3 and estrogen receptor positivity

rejected.label: Extramammary Paget Disease
rejected.why: Absence of typical pagetoid cells and lack of epidermal involvement

rejected.label: Sweat gland carcinoma
rejected.why: Presence of apocrine glands and GATA3 positivity suggests a more specific diagnosis

rejected.label: Carcinoma of mammary-like gland
rejected.why: Less specific diagnosis compared to primary invasive lobular breast carcinoma in heterotopic cutaneous breast tissue
